title: Marimba
reference_instrument: Iowa MIS marimba (model NA; bar material not stated; yarn, cord and rubber mallets)
summary: A struck rosewood bar, not yet a marimba: A3, Gb2, Eb6 and the scale's eight notes, C4 to C5, have a resonator tube, the hard rubber mallet isn't the recording's, and the undercut is solved in the engine and not measured. Those eleven notes now take the bar's loss from one printed whole-bar loss factor, eta 0.0045 from H. Hill's unrefereed 2011 student report, tried after seeing that the notes decayed too fast on a law fit through three printed rosewood bars, and f1 now decays far closer to the recordings: on A3 its two lines each fall at 48 dB/s (70 and 71 on the earlier law) against the recording's 31.4, on C5 the line that stays at 77.2 (129.7) against 59.7, and on Gb2 f1 now lasts longer than the recording's, 12.1 dB/s against 21.9. On every note the tube makes the line that stays fall faster than the bar's own law. On Eb6 f1 falls 168.9 dB/s, against 348.8 on the earlier law without a tube, and its recording is a roll that gives no decay to compare. The outline comes from J. La Favre's table of an unnamed commercial 5-octave marimba, and the stiffness and density from the rosewood row of Chaigne and Doutaut 1997. Iowa states no bar wood or outline, so this isn't the recording's bar. A3 is a bright knock, its 2017 Hz mode within 40 dB of f1 for about 180 ms while f1 swells for 171 ms from the strike. Eb6 is close to one decaying sine, set against a recording that is a roll. On Gb2 f1 is the strongest line, 6.6 dB over the bar's third bending mode; the recording's f1 leads its third mode by 31 dB. Gb2, C5 and Eb6 hear the bar through the broadband observer, which holds during the mallet's contact, and there the contact stands too strong against each recording's first millisecond, by 12.8 dB on Gb2 and 10.2 on C5; Eb6's recording is a roll, whose first millisecond can't judge it. A3's page, restored on 2026-11-10 to a render as good as the best this note has had on the grader, hears the bar through the narrow-band law, which passes the contact force as a pulse, and by the same read its contact stands 5.3 dB too strong; the page it replaced carried the observer, which on one build adds 0.09 to A3's total distance to the recording.
physics_present: The bar outline from J. La Favre's table of an unnamed commercial 5-octave marimba with rosewood bars, on a 56 x 6 x 3 mesh, and G4 on 56 x 6 x 4, A4 on 56 x 8 x 5, B4 on 56 x 8 x 6, C5 on 56 x 8 x 4 and Eb6 on 56 x 12 x 6, each with its cut solved again there, because origin's boundary-element floor refuses the coarser mesh at their bands. On Eb6 each grid face of the bar's radiating surface is split along its shorter diagonal (origin 9d2b77819), so all 15 modes under its card's 10000 Hz band are kept

Rosewood stiffness and density from Chaigne and Doutaut 1997 (JASA 101, Table I): E 2.13e10, density 1015. The other elastic ratios are, on Gb2, C5 and Eb6, those of a C3 marimba bar's rosewood as Beaton and Scavone 2021 (Table II) print them from Bork et al. 1999, with the undercut solved again on them; on A3, Honduras mahogany's, a stand-in (USDA Wood Handbook)

The bar's loss on A3, Gb2, C4 to C5 and Eb6: one printed whole-bar loss factor, eta 0.0045 at every mode, 1/tau = pi eta f, the mean as printed, with the printed range 0.0036 to 0.0068 as its limit. It is from H. Hill's unrefereed 2011 student report (NSF REU, University of Illinois Physics 406): the bars of a Yamaha YM-5100A, Honduras rosewood per the maker's spec for that model, recorded in a room with the resonators off, so eta holds the wood, the cord and the bar's own radiation, and the tube adds only its own losses. The stiffness and density stay Chaigne and Doutaut's, so the loss and the stiffness come from different rosewoods. It was tried after seeing that the notes decay too fast on the earlier law, and no recording number entered it. Hill measured the six C bars, C2 to C7, so every f1 here lies inside that span

A circular-arc undercut solved in the engine from the modes alone, for f1 at equal temperament and f2 = 4 f1, the tuning the builder states for its own padouk bars; the third mode isn't aimed at. On Eb6 the arch length is the one the builder prints on its padouk table and only f1 is solved, because the builder says that register is tuned to the fundamental only. On Gb2 the arc runs to the blank's length limit and only its middle is solved, for f1 alone, leaving 5.498 mm of 23.37 mm; f2/f1 comes out 3.991, untargeted
A Hertz contact mallet, Chaigne and Doutaut's hard rubber row at 1.0 m/s, with the strike point carried from the xylophone bar
Burton-Miller boundary-element radiation up to the band each page states, with no box, heard through the broadband observer on Gb2, C5 and Eb6 and through the narrow-band law on A3

The broadband observer on Gb2, C5 and Eb6 (e6313e19d): the boundary elements' transfer from each bar mode to the microphone, fitted as one delay and a rational part of order 16 within its 5 % budget on held-out frequencies (3.96 % on Eb6, 0.72 % or less on the rest), driven by a one-way copy of the bar's modes, so it moves nothing in the bar. It holds during the mallet's contact, where the narrow-band law it replaced passed the contact force as a pulse: on C5 a second receiver 27.68 mm further out hears one delayed wave during the contact, to a residual 59.4 dB under, where the narrow-band pair leaves one only 3.6 dB under. It hears the bar's travel time, 2.92 to 2.93 ms to the microphone, with the tube's mouth at 3.05 to 3.09 ms, so each onset is the bar's arrival. Each run of the wave that brought it also kept the narrow-band file, and on every page of that wave that file was the earlier page's clip byte for byte. A3's page was restored on 2026-11-10 to a render of A3's card from before the observer, as good as the best this note has had on the grader: 13 of 14 inside the real-vs-real ruler, strict 13, at a total distance of 9.40, against 9.49 for the observer page it replaced. It hears the bar through the narrow-band law, which passes the contact force as a pulse. On one build, with all else the same, the observer's four rows add 0.09 to A3's total distance: the cepstral envelope, the attack and the short-time spectrum move further from the recording, and the centroid and the wavelet spectrum closer. The observer stays in the code and on the other marimba cards

On A3, Gb2, Eb6 and the scale's eight notes, C4 to C5, a closed tube under the bar, coupled both ways: La Favre's tube for that note, from La Favre's own padouk marimba, not this bar's instrument, with its stop set to this bar and each bar mode exchanging with its nearest tube mode alone. On Hill's loss the tube's first mode loses more than the bar on every one of them, and on Gb2 and C4 to C5 by more than the coupling can bridge, so f1 is one frequency with two decays; on A3 the two lines still split, by 0.28 Hz, and start nearly opposite in phase, so f1's band has no dip before it is 130 dB under its peak. On B4 the stop's one solve leaves the tube's first resonance 0.06 Hz above f1, and on Eb6 0.124 Hz under it, because that solve carried the bar's reflection over from a probe at another stop and the render reads it again at the set one; the others are within 0.03 Hz. Eb6's tube has one mode under its band, so every bar mode exchanges with it, and its line is gone within the first 0.15 s, after which f1's band holds one line, 1244.39 Hz, falling 19.44 /s. La Favre prints no air column for Gb2's tube, only its total length, and La Favre's is mitered in 3 sections where this model's is straight
physics_missing: What the A3 recording's lines at 3.00, 5.00 and 7.00 f1 are: they fall at 50-52 dB/s where this tube's odd modes lose 334, 911 and 1952 dB/s by the printed laws, and on this render's clip the tube's lines sit 42 to 53 dB under them. At equal modal velocity A3's f1 radiates 32 dB less than its third mode

The recording's mallet: the Gb2, A3 and C5 recordings use a cord mallet, and Eb6's is a roll with no mallet named. The recordings differ in mallet as well as tube, and these renders can't separate the two. The hard rubber contact stands too strong against each recording's first millisecond, read on the served clips: with the broadband observer by 12.8 dB on Gb2 and 10.2 on C5, and through the narrow-band law on A3 by 5.3 dB. On Eb6 the first millisecond now peaks 3.2 dB under the ring's crest, 8.0 under before, which the roll can't judge

A felt mallet: one trial struck the Gb2 page's card with Rhaouti, Chaigne and Joly's measured timpani felt mallet as a stand-in for the rubber row, at the page's 1.0 m/s, outside that felt row's validity of 1.35 to 1.45 m/s. It scored 12 of 14 inside the real-vs-real ruler, where the page scores 14, with the cepstral envelope and the attack outside, and its brightness (centroid) fell to 93 Hz, on f1 itself, against the recording's 140 Hz (190 on the page, 183 before its receiver changed), so it was set aside and is on no page

The right decay: on Hill's loss f1 decays far closer to the recordings, but not onto them. On A3 its two lines each fall at 48 dB/s (70 and 71 on the earlier law) against the recording's band at 31.4; read the recording's way, from 100 ms past the band's peak, f1 falls 38.0 (64.2 on the earlier law), slower than either line because the lines come into phase across that read; on C5 the line that stays falls at 77.2 (129.7 on the earlier law) against 59.7; on Gb2 the f1 band falls 12.1 dB/s against the recording's 21.9 (22.9 on the earlier law), its two lines at 14.2 and 20.2, so f1 now lasts longer than the recording's. On the scale's eight notes the line that stays falls at 52 to 77 dB/s. On every note the tube makes it fall faster than the bar's own law, which gives 11.4 dB/s on Gb2, 27.0 on A3, 32 to 64 on C4 to C5 and 152.8 on Eb6. Chaigne and Doutaut write that marimba bars have lower internal damping and stronger tube coupling than xylophone bars, and that decay times with and without the tube clearly differ on marimbas in the low range. Nothing was aimed at the recordings: the stops sit on each bar's f1, the tube's loss is the printed laws' and the bar's is one printed number. On Eb6 f1 falls 168.9 dB/s (348.8 on the earlier law without a tube), but Eb6's recording is a roll, so it gives no decay to compare
A printed undercut: the rosewood table prints no arch length and no tuning, so it is not known that a maker would cut what the engine solved
The recording's bar: Iowa states no bar wood and no bar outline
Any mode above the band each page states. Above it a file holds only the contact as the observer hears the kept modes under the mallet: on Gb2 2.6 % of the file's energy, nearly all in its first 3 ms
